title: Optional dynamic batch size in the existing ONNX export method
body:
## Use case

The current ONNX export traces a batch of one. Batched evaluation or inference across multiple environments therefore requires custom export code, including different batch axes for recurrent hidden and cell states.

I propose an opt-in `dynamic_batch=False` argument on the existing `OnPolicyRunner.export_policy_to_onnx` method, targeting `extras`. Existing calls and fixed-batch exports would keep their current behavior; there would be no parallel exporter API.

## Proposed behavior

With `dynamic_batch=True`, observation/action tensors use batch axis 0, while recurrent hidden/cell inputs and outputs use axis 1. The implementation would reuse the existing `as_onnx()` wrappers and their named inputs/outputs. MLP, CNN, GRU and LSTM exports would keep feature dimensions, recurrent layer count and hidden size fixed.

The optional path would explicitly use the TorchScript ONNX exporter (`dynamo=False`) with dynamic axes. This is a deliberate, documented choice rather than an automatic fallback: the modern exporter fails on a dynamic LSTM in the package's minimum supported PyTorch 2.6 (`Cannot call numel() on tensor with symbolic sizes/strides`). The default export path would not change. Current PyTorch deprecates the legacy exporter, so its suitability for this optional feature is a design consideration.

## Initial evidence

A local prototype has exported MLP, CNN, two-layer GRU and two-layer LSTM models with the explicit dynamic-axis route on both PyTorch 2.6.0 and 2.15.0. ONNX checker and strict shape inference pass. ONNX's local `ReferenceEvaluator` reproduces native actions and hidden/cell outputs at batch sizes 1, 3 and 7, with maximum absolute error below 2.4e-7. All batch input/output dimensions share the same symbolic name. No deployment-runtime compatibility or throughput improvement is claimed.

The proposed tests would exercise the public runner method, verify that default shapes stay fixed, and feed recurrent output states into a subsequent inference step. This is separate from the additional export format proposed in #269.

Would this small optional parameter fit the export API, or would you prefer to limit dynamic batching to a newer modern-exporter version? I can provide the tested implementation with the support boundary made explicit.

pr_title: Add optional dynamic batch size to ONNX policy export
pr_body:
## Use case

Batched policy evaluation currently needs custom ONNX export code, including different batch axes for recurrent states. This adds the opt-in `dynamic_batch=False` argument to the existing `OnPolicyRunner.export_policy_to_onnx` method, as proposed in #301.

## Changes

- With `dynamic_batch=True`, observation/image/action tensors use batch axis 0; GRU/LSTM hidden and cell tensors use axis 1. All share the `batch` symbol, while feature dimensions, image dimensions and recurrent layer/hidden dimensions stay fixed.
- The optional path explicitly selects `dynamo=False` and dynamic axes, reusing the current model wrappers. It has no exporter retry or version-dependent fallback.
- Omitting the argument preserves the existing fixed-batch export and exporter selection. The guide describes batched use and recurrent-state feedback.

The legacy route is deliberate: the modern exporter in PyTorch 2.6 fails on the tested dynamic LSTM with `Cannot call numel() on tensor with symbolic sizes/strides`. Current PyTorch deprecates the legacy exporter, so this limitation is documented. Deployment-runtime compatibility and throughput are outside the validation performed here.

## Validation

The public runner export method is exercised with MLP, CNN, two-layer GRU and two-layer LSTM policies. ONNX checker and strict shape inference verify static non-batch dimensions and the shared dynamic symbol. ONNX's local `ReferenceEvaluator` matches native actions and recurrent states at batch sizes 1, 3 and 7. Recurrent tests feed each exported state output into a second inference step. Default fixed-batch exports are also checked.

- Focused shape/numerical tests: 16 passed on PyTorch 2.6.0 and 16 passed on 2.15.0 (Python 3.12, ONNX 1.23.2).
- Local suite on PyTorch 2.6.0: 285 passed; pre-commit checks passed. Native Gloo tests run in remote CI.
- Feature ablation (the option accepted but dynamic axes disabled): [8 expected failures, 281 passes and 1 evaluator skip](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43917474967).
- Complete implementation: [all four Python 3.9–3.12 jobs passed](https://github.com/Afloat16/rsl_rl/actions/runs/43917724434); Python 3.12 ran 290 tests, and Python 3.9 ran 288 with 2 explicitly skipped LSTM numerical cases. The older ONNX reference evaluator omits the cell-state output; LSTM checker/shape tests still run there. Lint and documentation checks passed.

Closes #301. This extends the existing ONNX exporter; it is separate from the additional export format discussed in #269.
